liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Playin' in the Band** (1 review): The unusual opening song made the reviewer initially think they missed the first set [14]
- **Saint of Circumstance** (1 review): A great JG solo occurred during this track in the solid second set [20]
- **Not Fade Away** (1 review): Beautiful jamming occurred during this track, which the reviewer highlighted as a positive [18]
- **Good Lovin'** (1 review): A climactic BW vocal improv happened during this high-energy second set performance [20]
- **Touch of Grey** (1 review): The band encored with this song for the first time during the performance [17]

## The recordings

- **gd1982-09-15.134869.nak300.schley.flac2448** (recommended): matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 21 songs; 143 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [1]
- **gd1982-09-15.152348.beyer.m160.eaton.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 21 songs; 148 min [4]
- **gd1982-09-15.sbd-aud.cribbs.8550.sbefail.shnf**: soundboard; 22 songs; 137 min; rated 4.21/5 by 14 [8]. Said about its sound: The recording features a cool Playin' theme running throughout the performance [11]
- **gd1982-09-15.fob.tigerrose.howard.andrewf.81690.sbeok.flac16**: source not stated; 21 songs; 138 min; rated 4.56/5 by 9 [9]. Said about its sound: The first notes of this song are slightly clipped in the recording; A tape flip in this track cuts into the beginning of the subsequent jam [9]

## Around the show

- The reviewer favored Capital Centre as their most frequent venue for seeing the band [12]
- Reviewer drove a motorcycle from North Carolina, meeting friends in the parking lot [13]
- This was the reviewer's fifth show, having missed the closest Charlottesville date [13]
- Attendees passed around a large bag of caps and stems while driving late [14]
- Reviewer and a friend, new to the band, took Purple gels and waited hours for a car [16]
- Highlights bring a second set flavor to the first set, matching the previous UVA night [12]
- Reviewer prefers this show over most Spring 1982 dates, except for Berkeley and a few others [18]
- Fall 1982 setlists were noted as being heavy on Crazy Fingers and Playin' in the Band [19]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1982-09-15.134869.nak300.schley.flac2448**: taped by Brian Schley; transferred by Andrew F.; source: AUD: Nakamichi CM300/CP-4 shotguns > Sony TC-D5 > Maxell XLII. Set up inside SBD perimeter area for 1st Set, mics moved onto SBD platform for 2nd Set,… [1]. Also: Patches from ID-81690 and ID-118451 were applied to fix gaps in the recording [1]
- **gd1982-09-15.152348.beyer.m160.eaton.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Rob Eaton; transferred by Rob Eaton, Scott Clugston; source: Rob Eaton's Master Audience Cassettes; (3)Beyer M160 mics > Nakamichi 550 [4]. Also: Rob Eaton recorded and transferred the source, with Charlie Miller coordinating the effort [4]
- **gd1982-09-15.sbd-aud.cribbs.8550.sbefail.shnf**: taped by see notes; transferred by see notes; source: see notes [8]. Also: Jim Wise transferred the analog source, and Sean Cribbs normalized and encoded the file; Tiger Rose recorded the FOB section using Nak shotgun mics into a Sony TC-D5M [8]
- **gd1982-09-15.fob.tigerrose.howard.andrewf.81690.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Tiger Rose; transferred by David Howard and Andrew F; source: "Recorded by Tiger Rose, FOB Nak shotgun mics > Sony TC-D5. MAC > CD Analog to Digital transfer by David Howard." [9]
